text:
alice: Hey team — customer on enterprise plan reports OAuth login failing intermittently. They do Google OIDC + mobile webview. Error: "state mismatch / PKCE_verifier missing" after redirect. Anyone seen a proxy that rewrites hash fragments?

sam: can you paste the exact redirect URL they're getting back to us?

alice: here's the URL the mobile app posted to our callback (redacted):
```
https://app.customer.example/callback%23state=xyz123&session=abc
```
Note: client initiates auth with redirect_uri=https://app.customer.example/callback#app-state (they used fragment to preserve deep link state).

liz: ugh, that %23 means the proxy or LB encoded the '#' into the path. Browser/webview should never send the fragment to server, but if a proxy rewrites the URL it can end up in the request path and our callback parser sees it as part of the path/query. That will break PKCE/state handling.

sam: do we have nginx / cloudfront logs showing the raw request line?

alice: attached logs from their partner network (redacted):
```
GET /callback%23state=xyz123?code=CODE123 HTTP/1.1
Host: app.customer.example
User-Agent: AndroidWebView/1.0
```

liz: yep that's the symptom. Our callback expects state in query param (state=...), but client put it in fragment. When the proxy encodes '#', it becomes path-encoded and we get a bad state value.

tim: two options: (1) short-term: try to be tolerant in our callback and detect %23 or encoded fragment and URL-decode/repair before validating state. (2) long-term: update docs/quickstart to strongly discourage putting state in fragment; advise using OIDC response_mode=form_post or include state in redirect query param.

alice: customer wants a hotfix. Can we implement a tolerant decode in callback handler? small patch?

liz: minimal patch idea (Node/Express):
```
// pseudo
let path = req.originalUrl;
if (path.includes('%23')) {
  path = decodeURIComponent(path);
  // extract state from decoded tail
}
```
Doable but risky: could mask other issues or open an odd redirect attack vector. Need code review.

sam: also check we aren't accidentally normalizing paths earlier in our proxy that strips fragments. If we accept decoded fragment, ensure we canonicalize and enforce same-origin redirect_uri check.

infra-bot: created ticket #INF-4123: investigate callback tolerant decode; assigned to eng-oncall. ETA 48h for patch + canary.

alice: customer on Dedicated plan; they asked for hotfix within 48h. Escalating to SRE + account.

tim: I'll open a PR that only decodes a single trailing %23 sequence and extracts any state-like token, with strict validation and logging. If logs show repeated incidents we can revisit.

liz: also ping product to update quickstart and best-practice: don't use fragments for PKCE/state for server callbacks. Provide sample with response_mode=form_post and mobile deep link flow.

alice: thanks. I'll coordinate with account team and share workaround to customer: switch to query-param state or set response_mode=form_post.

sam: noted. follow-up: we should add a regression test simulating encoded-fragment callback and ensure we log the decode attempt (no silent fixes).

alice: closing loop for now — will post updates in this thread when PR is live. :thumbsup:
